metadata.source: IRI / Columbia Climate School & NOAA CPC ENSO Prediction Plume
metadata.discussion:
The mid-August 2026 CCSR/IRI ENSO prediction plume has been updated with the latest model forecasts. The outlook shows strong agreement among the 26 participating models (15 dynamical and 11 statistical) that El Niño conditions will strengthen further during 2026 and persist into early 2027. All models maintain positive Niño3.4 anomalies throughout the forecast period, indicating a high level of confidence in the ongoing warming of the central and eastern tropical Pacific. Almost all dynamical and statistical models forecast Niño3.4 anomalies exceeding +2.0°C in Aug-Oct, indicative of a very strong event. Despite some uncertainty in the projected peak intensity, the forecast consensus is clear: a strong El Niño is highly likely to develop and persist through late 2026.

To generate the ENSO probability outlook, forecasts from all 26 participating models (14 dynamical and 12 statistical) are combined into an equally weighted multi-model average of Niño3.4 SST anomalies. A Gaussian error distribution is then applied to the ensemble-mean forecast, with its width determined by the expected forecast skill for the season and lead time. Higher forecast skill results in a narrower distribution and greater confidence, while lower skill produces a broader range of possible outcomes. Probabilities are calculated based on the likelihood of Niño3.4 SST anomalies falling within the standard ENSO thresholds: El Niño (≥ +0.5°C), ENSO-neutral (-0.5°C to +0.5°C), and La Niña (≤ -0.5°C). This methodology translates the multi-model forecast into probabilities for each ENSO category.

The August 2026 outlook strongly favors the persistence of El Niño through early 2027. El Niño probabilities remain at 100% from ASO 2026 through FMA 2027, followed by 97% in MAM 2027, before declining to 78% in AMJ 2027. This sharp decline in probability during boreal spring is consistent with the tendency for strong El Niño events to weaken rapidly following their peak.

Notably, no probability is assigned to either La Niña or ENSO-neutral conditions from ASO 2026 through FMA 2027, underscoring the near-certainty of continued El Niño conditions through the remainder of 2026 and into early 2027. With the boreal spring predictability barrier now behind us, the persistence signal is particularly robust: strong model consensus and the absence of competing ENSO states point to near certainty that El Niño will persist into early 2027. The accompanying probability plot summarizes the forecast evolution and the changing likelihood of each ENSO phase throughout the forecast period.

current._histogramDoc: Auto-derived, not bundled: with histogram=null the frontend fits a Gaussian to this file's `models` each render (share of Dynamical+Statistical models in each ±0.5 °C Niño-3.4 tercile) so the bars update automatically every refresh — no manual entry. Within ~1% of IRI's published figure (their proprietary skill-weighted regression can't be reproduced exactly). To pin an exact match instead, hand-enter IRI's published values here as a [{season,nina,neutral,nino}] array.
